# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 7
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [dark]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[red] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✊ 👉 ☝ 👈 ✌ 👇 🤟 👉 👌 👇 🖐 👈 👆]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👈 ☝ 👇 ✌ 👉 🤟 👆]

**What I have and what I know.** My letter-code lessons from Mute have expired from my memory (they were taught more than three turns ago), which is why I could only wait through the long letter messages at turns 5–6. But Mute has just re-sent, verbatim, the two self-contained tables I *can* read: the five-pair table (count↔pointer: 1↔👉, 2↔👈, 3↔👇, 4↔👉, 5↔👇, trailing 👈) and the three-pair table (pointer↔wire: 👈↔1, 👇↔2, 👉↔3). Combined with my decoded rule "COUNT YELLOWS UNTIL DARK THEN CUT PAIRED," the natural read is: count→pointer, pointer→wire.

**The count.** The light went yellow at turn 1 and yellow again at turn 4 (green t2–t3), green t5, dark t6, and it is *still* dark now at t7. So yellows before first dark = 2 → pointer 👈 → wire 1 → **GREEN, leftmost**. But the count could instead mean only the final cycle's yellow (=1 → 👉 → BLUE), or the three-pair table could be the rule itself (2→👇→RED). Three defensible answers, one bomb, no second attempt — so I do not order a cut on a coin flip. Mute answers within one round; the dark has already persisted two turns, so one confirmation round is the right trade.

**Coordination path.** Blind hears my speech but can't hear Mute and can't see gestures; Mute hears everything but can only gesture back. So Blind's tactile report must go by voice to Mute, and Mute must relay it to me in thumbs/pointers/finger-counts — I'm defining that minimal protocol explicitly now, since my letter cipher is gone.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, important: your letter code expired from my memory more than three turns ago, and old messages are erased for me too. I could only read your two pointer tables, which I still hold. New protocol from now, gestures only: thumbs up yes, thumbs down no, one single pointer names the wire to cut — left pointer wire one green leftmost, down pointer wire two red middle, right pointer wire three blue rightmost — and finger counts are numbers: ☝ one, ✌ two, 🤟 three, 👌 four, 🖐 five. Facts from my side: light yellow turn one, green two, green three, yellow four, green five, dark six, dark again now turn seven; display zero throughout. Answer each question with one gesture, in order. One: is the rule — count ALL yellow phases until the light first goes dark, then cut the wire paired to that count via your five-pair table then your three-pair table? Two: that gives count two, pair two is left pointer, left is wire one, so Blind cuts the GREEN wire — thumbs up if yes, or send one single pointer for the correct wire. Three: if instead only the last cycle's yellow counts, the count is one and the wire is BLUE — thumbs up if BLUE is correct, thumbs down if not. Four: must the cut happen while dark, and does dark end and cycle back to yellow — thumbs up if the cut must be during dark, thumbs down if anytime, add a finger count if there is a turn limit. Five: does the display reading zero matter to the rule — up if yes, down if irrelevant. Six: has the bomb been touched at all yet — up if untouched. Blind will report by voice to you; relay his report to me using only this simple protocol.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, status: the indicator light has now been DARK for two straight turns and the display still reads zero. Nobody has been ordered to cut. Standing order unchanged: do not touch the bomb until you hear the exact phrase CUT WIRE ONE, CUT WIRE TWO, or CUT WIRE THREE — then cut exactly that one wire: one is green leftmost, two is red middle, three is blue rightmost. I expect to give that order within a round or two, once Mute confirms the wire. Do two things now. First, gesture me the number of wires you feel: three fingers 🤟 if three, or that many fingers if different. Second, speak a full tactile report aloud for Mute — I am deaf, Mute hears you and will relay it: how many wires and their order left to right, any texture, ridges, braille, numbers or labels you can feel, whether there is a cutter tool or whether you must pull, and whether anything else on the casing moves or clicks. Also confirm with a gesture to me: thumbs up if you have still not touched the bomb, thumbs down if you have.")
```

TURN 8
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [dark]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[red] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👇 👎 👍 👎 👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ 👇 ✌ 👇]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [🤟]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]

**Decoding Mute's answers, slot by slot against the protocol I gave last turn.** Message one had exactly six gestures for my six questions: [👍 👇 👎 👍 👎 👍]. Q1 👍 — yes, the rule is "count all yellow phases until the light first goes dark, then cut the paired wire." Q2 👇 — instead of a thumbs-up he sent a single pointer, which in my protocol names the wire: down pointer = wire two = the RED middle wire. Q3 👎 — blue is wrong, confirming the count is not "last cycle only." Q4 👍 — the cut must happen during dark (and no finger count followed, so no turn limit was flagged). Q5 👎 — display zero is irrelevant. Q6 👍 — bomb still untouched. Message two [✌ 👇 ✌ 👇] reads "two → wire two," twice — an explicit double confirmation: count two pairs to wire two. **Blind's replies:** 🤟 = he feels three wires, matching what I see; 👍 = he has not touched the bomb. **Everything converges.** The light was yellow at turns 1 and 4, went dark at turn 6 and is still dark now — count 2 → wire 2, red, middle. The required dark phase is active, Mute (who holds the manual) has named the wire directly in my own protocol, and Blind has three fingers on three wires and is waiting for exactly the phrase. One more confirmation round would add nothing Mute hasn't already said twice, and dark may not last forever — so I give the cut order now.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Blind — final order, execute the moment you hear this: CUT WIRE TWO. That is the MIDDLE wire of the three you feel. Cut only that one wire and nothing else, now. Mute has confirmed by the manual: the light showed two yellow phases before it went dark, and two pairs to wire two. After the cut, touch nothing further on the bomb. Gesture me thumbs up if the cut is done, thumbs down if you could not do it. Then speak aloud, for Mute to relay to me: everything you sense — any sound, click, warmth, movement, or change under your fingers.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute — your answers received and decoded: rule confirmed, count two, wire two red middle, cut during dark, display irrelevant, bomb untouched. The cut order goes to Blind this round while the light is dark. If your manual contradicts wire two in any way, gesture me thumbs down immediately — otherwise stay silent. When Blind speaks his post-cut report aloud, relay it to me in our simple protocol: thumbs for yes and no, pointers for wires, finger counts for numbers. The tables and your answers made this decodable — thank you.")
```
